altivest-group.depositMethods: Bank cards, PayPal, Skrill, bank transfer
altivest-group.support: Around-the-clock claim; one bullet reads "7 customer support"
intro: The marketing for Altivest Group promises automation, accuracy and speed. Its own pages also carry placeholders, conflicting lists and claims no third party verifies. This review keeps the pitch and the paperwork separate.
The desk combines AI signals with manual control. Newcomers can start on the practice account, fund US$300 when ready, and trade 12 assets through the partner broker.
The checks below follow the platform published pages in order - what it claims, what the fine print says, and where the two diverge. The verdict is a summary of those checks, nothing more.
whatItClaims: A partner broker holding funds and executing orders.
Withdrawals processed in under a day, per the page.
No prior trading experience required.
AI and algorithmic market analysis producing signals and suggested entries.
Automatic or manual execution, with a browser-based platform.
whatWeChecked: The payout promise: within-a-day wording without processing detail.
The broker relationship: which partner desk executes orders.
The asset list: how many pairs are actually offered.
The registration flow: what personal details the form collects.
The risk disclosure: where the capital-at-risk wording sits.
The security claims: encryption and account protection statements.

steps.title: Register
steps.text: Complete the short signup form and click the confirmation link in your inbox.

steps.title: Fund
steps.text: Send the US$300 starting deposit through one of the accepted methods.

steps.title: Configure
steps.text: Adjust the risk controls, pick a mode and practise on the demo before going live.

pros: No platform fees on top of spreads.
Risk settings before the first trade.
cons: No named regulator or licence.
Withdrawal fees the page omits.
Support channels not clearly listed.
Marketing numbers that the fine print walks back.
redFlags: The fee that is not a fee: spreads embedded in every trade.
Restriction lists that name different countries.
Payout promises with no processing detail.

faqs.a: The platform fee is absent, but every trade carries a broker spread the page itself calls the real cost. The headline says free; the fine print says otherwise. Budget for the fine print.

faqs.q: How much support does it offer?
faqs.a: Unclear - around-the-clock coverage is claimed, while other sections quote different figures. Ask support to reconcile them before you fund anything.

faqs.q: What does the published score actually mean?
faqs.a: It does double duty - a platform score and an early community response - and neither is independently verified. Treat both as marketing until proven otherwise.
The lists conflict - different sections of the site name different countries. Confirm your eligibility with support before depositing.

faqs.q: What happens after I sign up?
faqs.a: You confirm the account by email, fund US$300, set your risk preferences and choose automatic or manual mode. The demo account runs alongside while you learn.

bottomLine: Altivest Group is a standard-issue AI trading desk with the usual strengths and the usual omissions. None of the omissions are dealbreakers - they are conditions.
4.8 is our number, and it means the product works with conditions attached. The demo costs nothing; use it while the claims remain unproven.
